entity.help.chargeControl: The entity that starts and stops charging: a switch, a selector or a button. SpotNav uses it to follow the plan.
entity.help.currentLimit: The entity that reports the charger's current setpoint. Automatic uses the one SpotNav finds itself, for OCPP 0.12 chargers the session limit.
entity.help.energyRegister: Your charger's cumulative kWh meter. SpotNav uses it to know what has already been charged. Found automatically for OCPP chargers.
entity.help.powerEntity: For a charger behind a smart plug: the plug's power sensor, in W or kW. SpotNav counts the energy from it and sees when the car has stopped drawing. The plug must be rated for the charger's continuous current.
entity.help.vehicleSoc: The vehicle's charge level, read from the sensor chosen for the vehicle, or found automatically when it has only one.
entity.help.mainFuse: The site's main fuse in amperes. All chargers on the site together stay below it.
entity.help.importTarget: The hourly mean of import (kW) you want to stay under. Empty is off.
entity.help.safetyMargin: The current in amperes that SpotNav keeps free below the main fuse. Charging stays under the fuse minus this margin, so it must be below the fuse.
entity.help.measurementMode: Whether your meter reports each phase's current directly, or SpotNav works it out from power and voltage.
entity.help.voltageBetweenPhases: The voltage between two phases of your electrical installation. Three-phase charging power is figured from it.
entity.help.chargerPriority: When several chargers share the site's fuse, a charger set to First is served before the others and one set to Last gets what is left.
entity.help.phaseSwitching: When the sun does not cover three-phase charging, charge on one phase instead of drawing from the grid. While this is on, SpotNav sets the charger's phases itself and the charger's own automatic phase mode is not used. Some cars charge badly after a phase change: turn this off if your car stops charging.
entity.help.batteryPower: A sensor for the home battery's power, so SpotNav can take the battery into account.
entity.help.maxAge: How old a measurement may be, in seconds, before SpotNav stops trusting it.
entity.help.phaseDirect: The sensor that measures the current on this phase, in amperes.
entity.help.derivedPower: The sensor for active power on this phase.
entity.help.derivedReactivePower: The sensor for reactive power on this phase.
entity.help.derivedVoltage: The sensor for voltage on this phase.
entity.field.gridPowerInverted: The sensor shows export as positive
entity.field.batteryPowerInverted: The sensor shows discharge as positive
entity.help.siteCurrentSigned: Turn on if the meter reports a negative current while exporting. SpotNav then uses the size of the current, which is what loads the fuse, instead of rejecting it.
entity.help.gridPowerInverted: Turn on if the meter's power is positive while exporting (Huawei, SolarEdge, GoodWe and similar). SpotNav then reads import as positive. It also applies to the total grid power.
entity.help.gridPowerSource: Needed for solar and hybrid charging, and for full load balancing, when the phases only report current.
entity.help.gridPowerSourceExport: Only if the meter reports import and export as two sensors: the field above is then the import and this is the export.
entity.help.batteryPowerInverted: Turn on if the battery's power is positive while discharging (Tesla, Fronius, Enphase, GoodWe and similar). SpotNav then reads charging as positive.
entity.help.batteryDischargePower: Only for a battery that reports charging and discharging as two sensors: this is the discharge one, and the battery power sensor above is the charge one.
entity.help.heatMeter: The heat pump's electricity use: a power or energy sensor. SpotNav looks for it in the Energy dashboard's individual devices by itself; choose it here only when it is not found. It is shown in the house card, nothing is controlled.
entity.help.derivedPowerExport: Only when the meter reports import and export as two sensors: the power sensor above is then import and this one is export.
entity.help.derivedTwoSensors: One export sensor per phase. If your meter has no export per phase, keep one sensor with direction.

entity.help.derivedCurrent: The meter's own current on this phase. With it the current is exact.

site.activeControl.reason.directionUnkno: Load balancing cannot tell whether a phase draws from the grid or exports. It still lowers the car on an overload and raises it again within the room the measured current leaves, but cannot count export on a phase as room. Turn on “Grid current is signed” and choose the total grid power, or press Use on your meter under Found in Home Assistant.

Load balancing cannot tell whether a phase draws from the grid or exports. It still lowers the car on an overload and raises it again within the room the measured current leaves, but cannot count export on a phase as room. Your meter also reports power per phase, which gives the direction: press Use on your meter under Found in Home Assistant.

Your meter reports the current without a direction, so load balancing cannot tell whether a phase draws from the grid or exports. It still lowers the car on an overload and raises it again within the room the measured current leaves, but cannot count export on a phase as room.

beta.label: Beta tester
beta.more.gets: As a beta tester, control that otherwise waits until SpotNav has learned your home can start at once, a home battery brand not yet tested on site leaves shadow mode so its check can run, and you can run a hardware test.
beta.more.sent: While the box is ticked, the same redacted file as "Send debug info" is sent to SpotNav's developer once a night, for 14 days. Then the box unticks itself. Untick it at any time and nothing more is sent.
beta.more.email: The e-mail address is optional and only used to tell you about a problem we saw in your reports, or a fix for it. Reports and the address are kept for 90 days.
beta.more.never: Never skipped: the fuse limits (with the learned house peak, or a cautious default until it is learned), the write limits, the battery's own check, your acknowledgements, the heating's safety rules and a hot-water boost you started.
beta.more.test: The hardware test is started by you, at most once a day. It briefly holds, charges and discharges the home battery and engages the heating, then hands everything back. It takes at most ten minutes and costs at most a few kronor of grid energy.

battery.haDown.label: If Home Assistant stops
battery.haDown.offer: Grid charging of the home battery is held to at most {kw} kW, so the main fuse holds even if Home Assistant stops mid-charge. If you accept the risk, it may go up to what the fuse allows with an empty house.
battery.haDown.accepted: Accepted that a fuse may trip if Home Assistant stops or loses contact with the battery or the grid meter during a grid charge of the home battery. Only an administrator can change this.
battery.haDown.title: If Home Assistant stops during a grid charge of the home battery
battery.haDown.text: SpotNav protects the main fuse by reading the phases every 10 seconds and lowering the battery's charge when the house draws more. If Home Assistant stops (an update, a server outage, an error) or loses contact with the battery or the grid meter, nothing lowers it: the battery keeps charging at the power it was last given until Home Assistant can lower it again. If the house draws a lot meanwhile, a phase can go over the main fuse.
battery.haDown.worst: The worst that normally happens is that the main fuse trips and the house loses power until you reset or replace it.
battery.haDown.needs: It takes Home Assistant stopping or losing contact with the battery or the grid meter during a grid charge of the home battery, and the house drawing a lot before that is over.
battery.haDown.without: Without this acceptance, SpotNav grid-charges the home battery only as much as holds even in the worst case – on a 16–20 A fuse often almost nothing.
battery.haDown.check: I understand and accept that a fuse may trip if Home Assistant stops or loses contact with the battery or the grid meter during a grid charge of the home battery.
battery.cap.zero: No charging from the grid: the house can reach the fuse by itself ({rule}).
battery.cap.importLimit: The plant's own import limit protects the fuse when charging from the grid.
battery.cap.importLimitTotal: The plant's own import limit ({kw} kW) protects the fuse when charging from the grid. It limits the total over the three phases, so it is set lower than the fuse: one phase can carry the house's peak alone.
battery.cap.importLimitTooHigh: The plant's import limit reads {value} kW. It limits the total over the three phases, not each phase, so it protects the fuse only at {max} kW or less: one phase can carry the house's peak alone.
battery.cap.importLimitUnset: The plant's import limit limits the total over the three phases, not each phase. It protects the fuse when set to {max} kW or less: one phase can carry the house's peak alone.
battery.cap.importLimitPhase: Sigenergy holds each phase under {phase} kW (the plant's import limit, {kw} kW, shared over three phases): grid charging uses what the house leaves.
battery.cap.phase.notSaidToAct: Sigenergy can hold each phase under the plant's own import limit, and it is already set low enough for your main fuse. Grid charging then no longer has to be held back to protect the fuse if Home Assistant stops.
battery.cap.phase.outputTypeUnread: SpotNav cannot read the plant's Output Type. Enable that entity in the Sigenergy integration, so grid charging can rely on the plant's limit per phase.
battery.cap.phase.phaseControlOff: Independent phase power control is off or cannot be read. Turn it on (enable the entity in the Sigenergy integration first if it is disabled): then the plant holds each phase under its import limit.
battery.cap.phase.gridSensorOffline: The plant's grid sensor does not read as connected. Enable its status entity in the Sigenergy integration if it is disabled, otherwise check the grid sensor: the import limit works from it.
battery.cap.phase.firmwareNotTested: Sigenergy's import limit per phase has only been tested on another firmware than your plant runs now. Until the import-limit test has been run on this firmware, grid charging stays held back to protect the main fuse if Home Assistant stops.
battery.cap.phase.firmwareUnread: SpotNav cannot read the plant's firmware, so it cannot tell whether the import limit per phase has been tested on it. Enable the firmware entity in the Sigenergy integration if it is disabled; until then grid charging stays held back to protect the main fuse.
battery.cap.phase.limitTooHigh: Sigenergy can hold each phase under the plant's own import limit, but it reads {value} kW. At {max} kW or less it protects the main fuse even if Home Assistant stops, and grid charging is no longer held back.
battery.cap.phase.limitUnset: Sigenergy can hold each phase under the plant's own import limit, but it is not set. At {max} kW or less it protects the main fuse even if Home Assistant stops, and grid charging is no longer held back.
battery.cap.phase.setFailed: The import limit could not be set or confirmed yet. Wait a minute and try again, or set it in the Sigenergy app.
battery.cap.phase.setInApp: Set it in the Sigenergy app.
battery.cap.phase.checked: Before every grid charge SpotNav reads the limit and the plant's settings, and holds the charge back as before as soon as anything does not match.
battery.cap.phase.setText: SpotNav sets Sigenergy's import limit to {max} kW and then relies on it to hold each phase under the main fuse, even if Home Assistant stops. SpotNav never raises the limit. It shows, and can be changed, in the Sigenergy app.
battery.cap.phase.turnOnText: SpotNav relies on Sigenergy's import limit ({value} kW) to hold each phase under the main fuse, even if Home Assistant stops, and stops holding grid charging back to protect the fuse.

battery.perPhase.charging: Grid charging per phase: L1 {l1} kW · L2 {l2} kW · L3 {l3} kW

battery.cap.rule.learning: while the house's peaks are being learned

battery.preheat.disabled: The battery's cells are cold ({temp} °C). Its preheating switch “{name}” is disabled in Home Assistant, so SpotNav cannot see whether it is on. Enable it on the battery's device.

battery.error.generic: That did not work. Try again.
battery.error.notAdmin: Only an administrator can change this.

setup.heat.text: A heat pump was found. Set up heating, and SpotNav shows what it costs and when it runs.
state.houseCardStart: A home without a charger starts with the “SpotNav house” card instead: its settings hold the battery, heating and price.

hist.heat.shadowLine: Would have moved {kwh} out of {hours} expensive hours over {days} days.

hist.heat.runsNote: Told from the energy alone (no tank sensor): a run well above the usual small one is a draw, about its size the tank cooling while nobody drew.
hist.heat.noRuns: No hot-water run found this day.
